pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we differentiate a short story from a novel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the features of a short story for information
2. write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression
3. recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – SHORT STORY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – SHORT STORY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the features of a short story for information

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the features of a short story for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the features of a short story for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the features of a short story for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression

What this means
In this part you learn to write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the features of a short story for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story to a partner. (skill: write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the features of a short story for information.
3. Practise this skill: write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the place of short story writing in indigenous knowledge preservation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we differentiate a short story from a novel?
2. Why is it important for a community to honour its heroes and heroines?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the features of a short story for information.
5. Be able to: write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
